Geographically and temporally weighted regression

Source: R/spi.R
gtwreg.Rd

The regression of Kuo and Putra (2021, eqs 4-9), after Huang, Wu and Barry (2010): at each observation i the least-squares fit of all observations weighted by a Gaussian kernel of their space-time distance, so that the coefficients vary over places and periods. They relate robbery, domestic violence and fraud in the local government areas of New South Wales to the air quality index month by month.

Usage

gtwreg(
  y,
  x,
  u,
  v,
  t = NULL,
  h,
  tau = 0,
  crit = "cv",
  lonlat = FALSE,
  cons = TRUE
)

Arguments

y

The outcome: finite numbers.

x

The regressors: a numeric matrix or data frame, one row per value of y (columns named), or NULL for the constant alone.

u, v

The coordinates of each observation.

t

NULL or the time of each observation (numbers).

h

The bandwidths tried: positive numbers.

tau

The ratios of the time to the space scale tried: numbers from 0.

crit

"cv" or "aicc": how h and tau are chosen.

lonlat

TRUE for longitude and latitude in degrees.

cons

TRUE for a local constant.

Value

An object of class gtwreg, a list: coef and se, matrices of the local coefficients and their standard errors (one row per observation); fit, resid, hat and loo (the leave-one-out residuals); stat, a named vector (h, tau, rss, trs, trss, sigma2, cv, aicc, edf, r2); and grid, the criteria of every pair tried.

Details

With the spatial distance ds (planar, or kilometres on the sphere with lonlat) and the time distance dt, the space-time distance is d^2 = ds^2 + tau dt^2 (eq 7, the spatial scale set to 1) and the weight w = exp(-d^2 / h^2) (eq 8); beta_i = (X'W_i X)^-1 X'W_i y (eq 5). Without t (or with tau = 0) it is geographically weighted regression. The cross-validation score is sum (y_i - y_(-i))^2 (eq 9), the leave-one-out prediction from the fit at i without observation i (computed as e_i / (1 - S_ii), S the hat matrix). Kuo and Putra choose tau and the bandwidth h by cross-validation or by "the corrected Akaike information criterion" without giving it; the aicc here is the one of the GWR literature, n log(RSS / n) + n log(2 pi) + n (n + tr S) / (n - 2 - tr S). Give several values of h and tau and the pair with the smallest crit is fitted; all are in grid. The local standard errors are sigma^2 times the diagonal of (X'W_iX)^-1 X'W_i^2 X (X'W_iX)^-1, sigma^2 = RSS / (n - 2 tr S + tr S'S).

References

Kuo, P.-F. and Putra, I. G. B. (2021). Analyzing the relationship between air pollution and various types of crime. PLoS ONE, 16(8), e0255653. doi:10.1371/journal.pone.0255653

Huang, B., Wu, B. and Barry, M. (2010). Geographically and temporally weighted regression for modeling spatio-temporal variation in house prices. International Journal of Geographical Information Science, 24(3), 383-401. doi:10.1080/13658810802672469

See also

sarml(), gmoran()

Examples

set.seed(4)
d <- expand.grid(u = 1:6, v = 1:6, t = 1:4)
d$aqi <- rnorm(nrow(d))
d$y <- 1 + (0.2 + 0.1 * d$u) * d$aqi + rnorm(nrow(d), 0, 0.3)
r <- gtwreg(d$y, d["aqi"], d$u, d$v, d$t, h = c(1.5, 3, 6),
            tau = c(0, 1))
r
#> gtwreg: geographically and temporally weighted regression, h = 1.5, tau = 0
#> CV 13.488, AICc 70.291, R2 0.796, effective parameters 13.35
#> local coefficients (quartiles):
#>                0%       25%       50%       75%      100%
#> (const) 0.9361268 0.9679731 0.9848207 0.9955117 1.0355406
#> aqi     0.2981053 0.4329041 0.5922378 0.6711381 0.7942628
r$grid
#>     h tau       cv     aicc
#> 1 1.5   0 13.48802 70.29134
#> 2 3.0   0 14.16615 75.47577
#> 3 6.0   0 15.53506 88.76016
#> 4 1.5   1 13.72343 74.63537
#> 5 3.0   1 14.16584 75.13253
#> 6 6.0   1 15.53053 88.64167
